# Independent audit: arbitrary integer rank radial triangle descent

Source: `candidate 65cb1818e941a654`.
Full source, including the added explicit competing-source gap, audited

The independent checker `supporting computation verify_arbitrary_rank_radial_audit_slab_recovery.py`
also verifies actual polygon caps, all competing centroids in several
complete bases, and a noncoordinate rank-deficient lattice span.

## 1. Actual bodies, finite bases, and measure

The projection B is a full-dimensional compact convex body; the sampled
set P need only be centrally symmetric, not the entire projection B.
Positive continuous concavity of the radius produces a compact convex
body with nonempty ambient interior and exactly the fibers r_z T at
the COMPLETE integer base B intersect Z^n. Convexity uses 0 in T to
pass from a convexly combined radius to the larger concave radius.
All sampled fibers have positive planar area, so q=2 and the original
Hausdorff measure is exactly the finite sum of planar fiber areas.

The symmetry assumptions used later concern precisely the sampled
radii and P. No unasserted symmetry of the intervening real fibers
or the full projection is required. Rank-deficient P is allowed even
though B and the original body have nonempty full ambient interior.

## 2. Uniform finite-base bounded tilts

The source centroid is zero in continuous coordinates. A strict common
Euclidean support bound H exists for all nearby radial fibers. Splitting
the fixed finite difference rows d_z=z-z0 according to whether
|alpha.d_z|<=H produces a feasible closed polyhedron. Equalities preserve
every nonsaturated trace; inequalities at +/-H preserve actual full/empty
sets because the support bound is strict, not merely their areas.

The minimum-norm feasible beta exists by closedness and coercivity. If
a direction annihilates all equality rows and all active inequality rows,
both sufficiently small signs remain feasible; the finite inactive rows
have positive slack. Minimality thus puts beta in the active row span.
Choosing an independent row basis gives exactly

    beta=D^T(DD^T)^(-1)t.

There are finitely many possible row bases and |t_i|<=H, so their operator
norms give one finite bound KH. The rank-zero case gives beta=0. Taking
the maximum over finite source bases is valid. Invisible integer-normal
directions are removed in the fixed span and cannot produce a false
unbounded sequence or strict Hessian.

For fixed positive fibers, null limiting line boundaries imply continuity
on the resulting compact normal domain. Uniform continuity in the body
array is even stronger: nested homothetic triangles have symmetric-
difference area V|r_z^2-s_z^2|, so the source's bound (6) holds uniformly
over ALL fixed measurable halfspaces, independently of their tilts.

A vertical closed cap through a centroid cannot be cheaper: a sufficiently
large finite integer coefficient plus any nonzero continuous normal
preserves every strictly sided base and removes some of the old tied
full-fiber trace. At the own centroid that removal has positive area.
Thus a nonvertical attained minimum equals the all-ambient infimum.

## 3. Baseline all-normal and all-source certification

The complete ordinary triangle paired-depth theorem applies to each
reflected equal-radius pair independently for the actual common normal
and its actual integer threshold. Its sum plus the own triangle gives
Q0=2R0. The three cylindrical canonical caps attain Q0 and cover every
continuous fiber space, so they prove the global upper bound as well.

Equality first forces one of the three ordinary canonical centroid
directions in the positive own fiber. The exact paired-tail formulas
(9) are continuous at both transitions r and 2r, and exceed 4r^2 at
every nonzero displacement. Thus equality forces alpha.z=0 for ALL
z in P. Restricted to L this forces alpha=0. The three active traces
are therefore complete, including normals arbitrarily far from the
initial local charts after taking bounded representatives.

The determinant-one cyclic triangle map has I+A+A^2=0. Depth superlevel
sets are convex: for any containing halfspace at a convex combination,
one of the combined points lies in that halfspace. Orbit averaging
therefore bounds every point in a fixed fiber by its centroid's depth.

For a nonzero source base z0, the canonical tilted cap's exact mass is

    Q0 -2t S1|z0|^2 +(t^2/2)H2,

where S1=sum r_z, d_z=z0.(z-z0), and H2=sum d_z^2. The source's choice
t=min(r_min/(2J),S1|z0|^2/H2), J=max|d_z|, is positive because z=0
gives d_0=-|z0|^2. It has |t d_z|<=r_min/2, so every retained vertex
margin stays positive and every other vertex margin stays negative.
The actual proper-chamber formula is therefore applicable, giving the
strict decrease at least (3/2)t S1|z0|^2. A finite minimum supplies
a uniform gap at every nonzero base, and the uniform area estimate
preserves it nearby. Orbit averaging extends it to EVERY point there.

At base zero any nonzero continuous point has positive evaluation in
some canonical normal. Shifting that cap through the point removes a
positive own-fiber slab. Hence the baseline source is uniquely deepest.

## 4. Optimized normal branch and global persistence

The exact cap formula (12) follows by actual triangle edge intercepts.
Its square completion uses b in range G, and the positive quadratic
form G restricted to L. This gives optimized tilt -2G^dagger b, angle
zero, and mass 2E. The Hessian at the baseline is diag(G|L,R0), with
all eigenvalues positive. In fact E is positive for every positive
sampled array because its residual projection norm includes the unchanged
coordinate r_0 at z=0; the proof only needs positivity near the baseline.

The bounded representatives give one compact global normal set for all
nearby arrays. At the baseline its complement outside small neighborhoods
of the three complete minima has a strictly positive gap. Uniform cap
mass control preserves that gap. Within sufficiently small charts the
proper status and positive normal Hessian persist; the square-completed
formula identifies the unique local minimum. Shrinking the array
neighborhood keeps each displayed optimizer inside those charts. Thus
the three branches are genuinely all-normal minimizing traces nearby.

All nonzero-base gaps persist while 2E tends to Q0. At base zero the
three optimized caps still have balanced continuous normals and pass
through zero. For any nonzero point there, one of them can be shifted
through the point to strictly remove own-fiber area. This proves the
UNIQUE global source (0,0), not merely a unique centroid among bases.

## 5. Genuine slack groups and their ownership

Every nonzero source centroid has an attained nonvertical critical cap
with mass strictly below 2E. Its cyclic orbit keeps the same raw integer
coefficient and cap mass; its three continuous normals sum to zero and
span the plane. It is therefore an actual positive full-rank critical
circuit covering the entire continuous space at its own base. Assigning
each such group only its own base, plus the main group at zero, covers
all original fibers with actual slack in every auxiliary group.

Frozen baseline groups preserve exact incidence and coverage nearby,
but are correctly not asserted to remain critical. Reselecting an
attaining cap gives current critical groups without requiring a smooth
selection. Shared original planes retain a single parameter and mass.
Any auxiliary critical cap with alpha.z0<=0 would contain the deepest
source and have mass >=2E, a contradiction; hence the strict drift
sign alpha.z0>0 is valid in arbitrary rank.

## 6. Rank, normalized gain, and genuine affine directions

The common continuous homothety c^2=R0/E sends all actual caps to their
images after multiplying integer coefficients by c. It preserves lattice
bases, incidence, ownership, full dimensionality, and compatibility, and
scales all cap masses by c^2. The actual GLOBAL raw maximum becomes
Q0 exactly, and the area gain is V R0 W/E.

At an even baseline the Hessian is 2V m(v)^T G^dagger m(v), rank k
on the full sampled-array space, with precisely the stated moment-zero
kernel. This is the Hessian of the displayed functional, not an assertion
that all abstract sampled velocities are compatible. The k affine
directions are, however, genuinely compatible: adding a.z to r0 on the
entire compact projection preserves concavity and retains uniform positive
radius for sufficiently small a. Their moment and norm identities give
b=Ga, R=R0+a^TGa, E=R0, so each nonzero a in L gives a strict actual
fixed-depth mass increase without any scaling. Opposite bases lie in
the same lattice parity class, making these velocities separately
first-order volume-neutral in each such class.

For b=0 the normalized mass is EXACTLY unchanged; this is not just
second-order neutrality. Rank-zero P={0}, including n=0, reduces to the
ordinary triangle and has no fictitious tilt coordinates or slack groups.
For rank-deficient P every G^dagger operation is restricted to L; adding
components in L-perp changes no sampled cap trace.

All these results stay near the normalized-depth baseline 4/9. They
make no assertion that a hypothetical below-OC body has radial triangle
fibers, the indicated symmetry, or an admissible affine escape.
